input.strategy_title: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard accessibility fixes for the four audited core Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic remediates the keyboard-accessibility defects that the accessibility
audit found in the four core Dashboard flows: project creation, workbench
spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission. It delivers a Dashboard
in which each of these flows can be completed with keyboard alone — no focus
traps, no unreachable controls, and consistent visible focus indicators
throughout. This is the code deliverable of the keyboard conformance strategy;
the published conformance statement (VPAT) that reflects this fixed state is
tracked separately under the Documentation component.

## Scope

- Fix the audit-enumerated keyboard operability defects across the four audited
  flows: project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run
  submission.
- Eliminate focus loss in modals used by these flows: focus moves into the
  modal on open, remains trapped within it while open, is restored to the
  invoking control on close, and modals are dismissible via keyboard.
- Make every control reachable and operable in each audited flow (tab order,
  keyboard activation, no pointer-only interactions).
- Make focus indicators consistent across the audited flows (same visible
  styling convention for the same control types) and present on all focusable
  elements in those flows.
- Verify the four flows end-to-end with keyboard-only walkthroughs as part of
  the fix work; the audit report's per-flow defect list is the work list.

Out of scope (per strategy):

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require.
- Flows outside the four audited ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model
  deployment, pipeline run submission) can be completed start-to-finish using
  the keyboard alone, verified by a keyboard-only walkthrough of each flow.
- No focus traps or focus loss remain in the audited flows: modal focus is
  managed (enter, contain, restore) and focus is never dropped to the document
  body during any step of the four flows.
- No control in the audited flows is unreachable or inoperable by keyboard;
  every interactive element is focusable and activatable via keyboard.
- Focus indicators are visible and consistent across the audited flows — the
  same indicator convention applies to equivalent controls in all four flows,
  verified by inspection of each flow's focusable elements.
- Every defect enumerated in the audit report for the four flows is addressed
  or explicitly dispositioned in the epic's tracking.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1):** The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard,
  with no focus traps or unreachable controls — covered by this epic's
  keyboard-operability and modal focus-management scope.
- **HLR-2 (P1):** Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited
  flows — covered by this epic's focus-indicator consistency scope; bundled
  with HLR-1 because both are remediated in the same passes over the same
  flow components (see decomposition summary).

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs statement)

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation
to reflect the Dashboard keyboard-accessibility fixes once they are complete:
the VPAT (Voluntary Product Accessibility Template) conformance statement and
the product documentation's accessibility statement. Two public-sector
customers require an updated, published conformance statement before renewal,
so the published documentation is a first-class deliverable of the strategy,
not an incidental touch-up. The content must be technically reviewed against
the implemented state of the four audited flows so the published claims match
what was actually fixed.

## Scope

Content outline (authored inside this epic):

- **VPAT conformance statement:** update the existing VPAT to reflect the
  keyboard operability and focus-indicator conformance of the four audited
  core Dashboard flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment,
  pipeline run submission) after the fixes; state remaining limitations
  accurately (screen-reader semantics beyond the keyboard fixes and flows
  outside the four audited ones remain out of scope per the strategy).
- **Product docs accessibility statement:** update the published accessibility
  statement in the product documentation to reflect the fixed state, including
  any documented keyboard-navigation guidance for the audited flows.
- **Republish:** republish both artifacts through the Red Hat documentation
  process so the updated conformance statement is publicly available to
  customers.

This epic authors and publishes documentation content only; it makes no code
changes and covers only the conformance documentation named in the strategy
(the VPAT and the accessibility statement — not general documentation rewrite).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT is updated to accurately reflect the keyboard conformance state of
  the four audited flows after the fixes, with limitations stated accurately.
- The product documentation accessibility statement is updated to reflect the
  fixed state.
- Both artifacts are technically reviewed against the implemented fixes — an
  engineering reviewer confirms every conformance claim in the updated content
  matches the shipped behavior of the four audited flows — before publication.
- The updated VPAT and accessibility statement are republished and publicly
  available (published through the documentation pipeline, reachable at the
  customer-facing documentation location).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P2):** The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and
  product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect
  the fixed state, with technical review — this epic's entire scope.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9017

Parent strategy: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows

## Triage Outcome

Not below-threshold: although the code scope is confined to a single component
(Dashboard) and the audit enumerates the exact defects (no genuine unknowns),
the strategy spans two architecturally distinct work streams that warrant
separate PR review cycles — Dashboard code implementation (keyboard operability
and focus-indicator fixes) and substantive content authoring (VPAT rewrite and
product accessibility statement, HLR-3). Substantive documentation authoring is
a distinct work stream, so the multiple-work-streams escape condition applies
and the strategy proceeds to full decomposition.

Not docs-only: the Dashboard component requires code changes.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Keyboard accessibility fixes for the four audited core Dashboard flows | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs statement) | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P2 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001[RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 Dashboard keyboard fixes] --> E002[RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 VPAT and accessibility statement]
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 → RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Rule 11 (docs last) | The conformance documentation must describe the fixed state of the four flows, so the docs-authoring epic is blocked by every Implementation epic — here, the single Dashboard fixes epic. The docs content is derived from what was actually fixed. |

No other edges: the strategy contains exactly one code work stream (one
component, one owning team, one logical change — keyboard accessibility across
the four audited flows), so no further epic boundaries exist. No Investigation
epics: the strategy's Open Questions section states "None — the audit report
enumerates the exact defects per flow," so no unknown changes which epics exist
or what they do. No tiered delivery: no external dependencies.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Notes |
|-----|----------|---------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Four audited flows fully keyboard-operable, no focus traps, no unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 (bundled) | Bundled with HLR-1: consistent focus indicators are part of the same keyboard-operability fix over the same four flows and the same Dashboard UI surface — the audit's indicator findings and operability findings are remediated in the same passes over the same components. HLR-2 is not independently deferrable (indicator fixes without operability fixes would not satisfy the audit remediation), and splitting would force two passes over the same components. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | VPAT and product docs accessibility statement updated and republished with technical review; priority follows both the HLR label and the docs-authoring priority exception (strategy frontmatter priority `Normal` → P2). |

Full coverage: HLR-1, HLR-2, HLR-3 all mapped; no orphaned requirements.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections (non-blocking):** the strategy provides no
  Impacted Teams table, no Dependencies table, no formal Given/When/Then
  Acceptance Criteria with "measured by" clauses, and no Non-Functional
  Requirements section. Epic acceptance criteria were derived from the HLRs and
  the problem statement; per-epic ACs should be refined against the audit
  report's enumerated defects at implementation time.
- **Documentation owning team inferred:** the strategy names no team for the
  Documentation component and no architecture-context file exists for it. The
  docs epic is assigned to "RHOAI Documentation" by convention; confirm the
  actual owning team before scheduling.
- **Single-sweep size risk on RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 (conditional re-split
  trigger):** E001 is deliberately one epic — it is a single logical change
  (keyboard accessibility remediation) applied as one mechanical sweep over an
  enumerated surface (the four audited flows), remediating the audit's
  defect list in shared Dashboard UI components across passes that would
  otherwise be repeated if split. The strategy provides no effort estimate,
  so treat the audit report's per-flow defect count as the sizing input.
  Pre-agreed re-split trigger: if the audit's per-flow defect count (or the
  mid-flight defect backlog for any single flow) exceeds the sprint estimate
  for the whole sweep — i.e. one flow's remediation alone consumes more than

  (one epic per audited flow) along the four-flow seam, keeping HLR-1 and

  split: the shared components and indicator convention argue for one sweep.
- **Priority note:** both code HLRs are P1 while the strategy's frontmatter
  priority is `Normal`; no inversion is implied — the renewal-driven VPAT
  deadline couples the P2 docs epic to P1 fixes, but the docs epic does not
  push priority upstream (docs-authoring priority exception).

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — no external dependencies with uncertain timing. The VPAT
publication is gated only on the completion of the fixes it documents.
